name: PT Sariguna Primatirta Tbk

frontmatter.title: Sariguna Primatirta: the index bid leaves in December, the growth does not
frontmatter.summary: FTSE deletes CLEO on 21 December, the last index bid for a stock the controller already owns almost entirely. The operating forecast is unchanged: revenue grows about three times the category, capex is near a fifth of sales, free cash flow is near nil. We rebase the multiple cross-checks to the de-rated peer level, which cuts the target to the share price. HOLD.
thesis: The category grows at a mid single-digit rate; CLEO has grown roughly three times faster, and the mechanism is physical - a national plant network feeding hundreds of internal nodes.
Gross margin fell sharply in 2026 and we assume a partial recovery, not a return to the FY2024 peak, because mix is shifting toward lower-margin single-serve.
Free cash flow is temporarily nil: capex peaks near a fifth of revenue and the incremental return is only modestly above the cost of capital, which is why the cash flow sits below price.

The flow backdrop is dated and adverse: HSC-listed, out of the IHSG since 13 November, deleted from the FTSE indices on 21 December, with a float below the exchange floor. It has not discounted the price below value - the shares still carry a premium to our fundamental value - so the call is a bet that part of that premium survives, not that it widens.

catalysts.event: FTSE Russell deletes CLEO, with thirteen other HSC-category names, from its global indices at the open; the last index demand for the float goes with it
FY2026 full-year results: the first clean read on full-year gross margin after the 2026 compression, and on capex against the plan
Free float must reach twelve and a half per cent of shares outstanding, the first step of the exchange's remedy - controller sell-down or new shares
MSCI decision on Indonesia's classification, the proposal being Standalone status; index increases for Indonesian names are frozen until then

blocks.text: **HOLD - target Rp369, total return 0.5% against a Rp370 share price.**

**What changed.** FTSE Russell deletes CLEO from its global indices at the open on 21 December 2026, one of fourteen Indonesian HSC-category names removed at the December review [S11]. No revenue line, cost, contract or asset depends on which index a share sits in; what moves is the marginal buyer. The company entered the exchange's high-shareholding-concentration list on 11 November, with ten holders owning 92.6% of the shares [S15], and left the IHSG calculation on 13 November [S13][S16]. December removes the passive bid for a float of 10.9% [S0].

**The multiples are rebased.** The two multiple cross-checks were an even blend of the peer median and this stock's own four-observation history - half of both inputs - and that history is entirely pre-de-rating: every observation is a year-end multiple struck before the 2026 regime turned [S0][S11][S15]. We drop it and strike both multiples at the peer median, the level at which the de-rated food complex clears on the same price date. The DCF is unchanged at Rp321 a share, the earnings multiple is Rp160 and the EBITDA multiple Rp217; the weighted blend is Rp278, which rolls forward to Rp306, the probability-weighted fundamental is Rp313, and the konglo lens takes it to the target of Rp369 - a total return of 0.5%, short of the ten per cent we require, so the call stays HOLD. The target is below the previous edition's because of this rebase alone; the operating forecast and the DCF are unchanged.

The price of Rp370 is 1.30 times the probability-weighted fundamental value of Rp283.8 [S0]. The lens keeps part of that gap and gives Rp369, above the twelve-month fundamental of Rp313: the HOLD is a bet that part of the premium survives, not a value call. Gross margin is what moves it - cost of goods sold of 1,213 IDR bn against nine-month sales of 2,626 IDR bn is several points worse than last year, and whether that unwinds is worth more than any plausible change in growth [S2][S9].

PT Sariguna Primatirta sells bottled drinking water through three reporting segments - bottle, non-bottle and other - trades food and beverage wholesale and makes industrial ice, under Cleo, VIO, Cleo Plantine, Anda and S-Tube, plus a ready-to-drink tea under NOGU. It was founded in 1988, listed in 2018 and sits under the Tancorp family's two vehicles - PT Tancorp Global Abadi, the larger holder, and PT Tancorp Global Sentosa, which the annual report names as the main and controlling shareholder - based in Sidoarjo [S4].

The mix explains the margin story: the bottle segment was 56.9% of nine-month net sales and grew 29.7% year on year, faster than the refill gallon and corporate formats in the non-bottle segment [S9][F9][F10]. Both grew; the bottle carries more resin and packaging per litre.

The footprint is the business: 33 factories, 500 internal distribution nodes and more than 12,000 distribution partners [S5][F11][F12][F22]. The count is reported as the sources report it: the July announcement [S8] said the three 2026 additions - Palu in the third quarter, Pontianak and Pekanbaru in the fourth - would take the network to thirty-two; the November report [S5] has thirty-three operating with Pekanbaru and Pontianak still to start before the year end [S5][S8]. Neither count drives capex. Each plant sits on a water source the group controls, which is what lets a company of this size compete on delivered cost rather than brand alone [S4].

The strategy builds plants and depots ahead of demand, accepting that opening them raises operating expense in the year it happens [S4 p.33]. Hence FY2025: revenue grew 4.8% where the plan called for twenty per cent, and profit fell where the plan called for growth [S4 p.99][F16].

The annual report puts category growth in a band topping out at 8.0% a year [S4 p.23] [F13]. The association is more bullish for 2026: GAPMMI expects food and beverage above six per cent, names bottled water among the double-digit growers and notes that many new plants and small producers are entering [S6][F18] - demand growing and supply responding at once.

Two forces favour scale. Mandatory SNI certification took effect in October 2026, with the Ministry of Industry funding technical assistance [S7][F17] - a fixed cost a national network spreads over tens of millions of cases, a single-plant operator cannot. And water is heavy and cheap, so delivered cost is dominated by distance from plant to shelf: 33 plants with 500 nodes can serve a store from nearer than a three-plant competitor [S5][F11][F12].

CLEO is the challenger, not the leader; brand perception is dominated by the two largest players [S6]. Growing the bottle segment at close to 29.7% against a mid single-digit category is share, not just demand [S9][S4 p.23]. The moat is distribution density and owned water sources, not pricing power: density is expensive to replicate, yet it does not protect the price line, because the product is undifferentiated to most consumers. Five forces: low substitute threat, moderate buyer and supplier power, high rivalry, and entry barriers that SNI compliance is raising [S6][S7].

The external influences we track are resin and packaging costs, which move with oil and the rupiah; the rupiah, which the house macro desk carries at 18,350 to the dollar in FY2027E; and weather, since a hot dry year lifts demand and 2026 was one [S4 p.30][S6]. The engine does not read the agricultural deck: both cost links are zeroed because CLEO buys PET resin, preforms and closures, not the cpo, soyoil, wheat, corn or soymeal complex [S2 p.7].

**Depreciation and history.** The data pack prints a charge for FY2025 and FY2024 barely half what the audited note allocates, because the direct-method cash flow reports a fraction of the real charge: 259 IDR bn in FY2025 and 208 IDR bn in FY2024 [S3 p.59][F1][F2]. Restating lifts FY2025 EBITDA to Rp806.4bn and FY2024 to Rp868.2bn, and every margin and multiple here uses the restated numbers; the same defect appears in the nine-month 2026 accounts (207 IDR bn) [S2 p.52]. **The definition.** EBITDA here is EBIT as reported plus the depreciation the notes allocate, which leaves the net other-income line inside EBIT; the company strips it, so its FY2025 EBITDA is IDR783bn [S8]. The difference is that net other income, about the size of the net other charge of Rp-22.8bn carried in every forecast year, so history is struck slightly above the company's line and the forecast slightly below it, and the ten per cent on the EBITDA multiple rests on the less flattering definition. Revenue has compounded at a high-teens rate from FY2022 to FY2025, with FY2025 the exception: growth of 4.8% and an EBITDA margin of 28.5% against 32.2%, as new plants ran ahead of the revenue they were built for [S3][S4 p.99].

**The current year.** Nine-month revenue was 2,626 IDR bn, up a quarter [S2 p.7][S9]. Cost of goods sold rose to 1,213 IDR bn, faster, so gross margin compressed by about three and a half points; selling expenses rose to 760 IDR bn and G&A to 132 IDR bn, both far more slowly, so the operating expense ratio fell by close to three points and absorbed most of the damage [S2]. Profit attributable was 368 IDR bn, up a fifth [S2][F4]: growth came from cost discipline, not pricing.

**Forecast.** FY2026E revenue growth of 24.1% is arithmetic rather than forecast: nine months are printed and the fourth quarter only has to grow a fifth. Growth then runs 15.5%, 13.0%, 11.0% and 9.0% before settling to 5.0%. The first-year fade is deliberate: FY2027E laps the heat-boosted 9M2026 base [S6][S9] even though the two fourth-quarter plants run for a full year, and the company's own twenty per cent plan was missed by a wide margin in FY2025 [S4 p.99][F16]. Gross margin starts at 53.4%, recovers to 54.6% by FY2030E and stays: a partial recovery, not a return to the FY2024 peak, because the mix shift into single-serve is structural [S9]. The mechanism is the three 2026 plants reaching utilisation, and the grid prices it a point either side. EBITDA margin returns to 28.5% by FY2030E, a shade above FY2025's 28.5%: the fall in the operating expense ratio is offset by a heavier depreciation charge as the plants enter service [S2].

**Cash flow and capital intensity.** Capex was Rp417.7bn in FY2025 and Rp583.8bn in FY2024, and nine-month 2026 cash capex of 385 IDR bn plus 131 IDR bn of advances puts FY2026E near Rp645.0bn, about a fifth of revenue [S3][S2]. Free cash flow to the firm is Rp151.5bn in FY2026E against profit of Rp468.3bn: the company earns accounting profit and spends it, converting only around FY2028E. Between FY2023 and FY2025 incremental after-tax EBIT over incremental net plant, intangibles and working capital sits in the low to mid teens; the terminal year earns the top of that range, so the growth we forecast is paid for, not declared [S3][S2].

**Balance sheet.** Debt was Rp426.8bn at the 2025 year end against cash of Rp32.3bn, so net debt to EBITDA is 0.5 [S3]: short-term working-capital and term loans and leases, no bond [S3 p.11][S2 p.5]. Nine-month operating cash flow covered the capex programme and the dividend, the balance from a small increase in borrowings [S2 p.9]. Growth is financed by retained earnings and a low payout, 15.7%, with the policy left to the annual meeting [S4 p.102].

**Earnings quality.** FY2025 passes most screens: operating cash flow exceeded net profit, so the accruals ratio is negative [S3]. September 2026 is where the screens change their answer: operating cash flow ran well ahead of profit of 368 IDR bn, but most of the gap is reversing timing - other payables to third parties rose above a hundred billion rupiah, taxes payable roughly quintupled and accrued expenses built [S2]. Receivables also outgrew revenue: third-party trade receivables went from 120 IDR bn at the 2025 year end to 188 IDR bn at 30 September 2026, roughly twice revenue growth [S2 p.4][S3 p.10] - real, and pointing at the auditor's inventory key audit matter, but second-order rather than manipulation-class [S3 p.5]. There is no capitalised development cost, no revaluation reserve, no monitoring-board status and no notation letter; related-party payables, the one flag, are sized in section six [S2][F8].

We value CLEO on a discounted cash flow, with earnings and EBITDA multiples as cross-checks: value here is a plant base that produces cash for decades, and in a year when capex is nearly triple depreciation any multiple of earnings says more about the capex cycle than the business [S3].

The cost of equity is 11.2% and the WACC 11.0%, inside the house rupiah band: a ten-year rupiah risk-free rate less the sovereign spread, the house consumer-staples beta (the pack carries no index series, so a measured beta cannot be fitted), a mature equity risk premium and an Indonesia country premium [S0], plus a 0.5% company premium, because beta prices market risk, not the risk in a register this controlled and this illiquid [S0][S10]. The WACC minus half a point row still lands below today's price.

The DCF gives Rp321 a share. Terminal value is 61.4% of enterprise value, high but normal at this horizon, and it is not doing the work of a re-rating: terminal capex sustains today's return rather than assuming it improves, and growth divided by that return needs about thirty-seven per cent of NOPAT reinvested, with terminal capex at 12.8% of sales against depreciation of 7.2% [S3].

Each cross-check is the peer median across the twenty-six FOOD_BEVERAGE tickers in the pack - the level at which the de-rated complex clears on the same price date [S0]. We weight them a fifth and a tenth and the DCF at seven-tenths.

**Why the own-history leg is gone.** The pack's own-history multiples are four annual observations to FY2025A, all struck before this year's regime turn: MSCI froze Indonesian index increases in January, the HSC list appeared on 11 November and the FTSE deletion takes effect on 21 December [S11][S15]. An even blend of that mean with the peer median is the multiple a premium franchise held before it de-rated, which the compounder card's de-rating base rate rules out as an input. The own post-de-rating window holds one observation, not a mean - 23.3x trailing earnings and 11.6x trailing EV/EBITDA at today's price - and we print it beside the peer median the model uses (10.1x earnings, 7.1x EV/EBITDA) rather than averaging it in. Both legs are struck on restated FY2025 [S3].

**The survival test.** The compounder card asks what exit multiple a target implies against the entry multiple, because a valuation that exits above the price it entered is multiple expansion wearing a cash-flow costume. Ours does the opposite in every leg. The target is 0.5% from the Rp370 price, so a buyer at the target pays today's 19.0x on FY2026E earnings and 9.8x on FY2026E EBITDA; two years out the same target is 13.0x and 6.9x, so being right needs the shares to keep de-rating, not to re-rate. The primary method goes further: its terminal value (61.4% of enterprise value) capitalises the terminal year's EBITDA at about a third below today's 9.8x and its EBIT about two-fifths below the equivalent entry multiple. No leg assumes multiple expansion; the mirror risk, that the de-rating runs past our terminal multiple, is what the peer-median cross-check prices.

**The divergence.** Both cross-checks sit below the DCF and well below the shares: the EV/EBITDA leg is -32.3% against the DCF - a 7.1x multiple on EBITDA struck before capex of IDR645.0bn against depreciation of IDR285.7bn, a gap of about a tenth of sales the equity holder funds and the multiple does not see - and the P/E leg -50.1% at 10.1x FY2025A earnings. On FY2026E figures the same legs sit more than two-fifths and about a third below today's price. That is what a peer-median benchmark means for a company growing at three times the category: it prices CLEO as the sector's median operator, which is why the multiples carry a fifth and a tenth of the weight and the DCF seven-tenths.
Growth compounds through a capital-heavy business while margin is a single-year flow; the discount rate dwarfs both.

**What the price implies.** The engine solves the reverse DCF on revenue growth and applies the solved increment to every forecast year, not FY2027E alone [S0]. Today's price implies 17.5% growth in FY2027E against our base of 15.5%, an increment of 1.99% added to every year. A one-year increment would lift the DCF by about a twenty-fifth; the engine's response is about a sixth, possible only if the increment is permanent. The market pays for a permanent step-up of about two points in every forecast year: a material premium, not the mild one the previous edition described.

**The konglo lens.** Ten holders own 92.6% of the shares, so a few per cent of the register sets the marginal price [S15]. The engine values the business first - Rp283.8 a share today, Rp313 in twelve months - and measures the price against the first: Rp370 over Rp283.8 is 1.30 times, a premium of roughly a third over what the methods say the business is worth [S0]. It then keeps a probability-weighted share of that gap: the base closes 40% of the log gap for Rp366, the bear 80% for Rp330, the bull assumes the premium re-widens for Rp413; weighted 50% base, 25% bear and 25% bull, that is Rp369 [S0].

The two flags work on the closing share, not on the target: they take the base case from the deck's 30% of the log gap to 40% - ten percentage points more, so less of the premium is kept and the target falls rather than rises. The flags are HSC membership [S15] and the 1.6 point free-float gap to the 12.5% step due by 31 March 2027 [S0][S10]; the FTSE deletion is not a third flag, being the same exclusion. Because the target sits above the twelve-month fundamental, a reader who believes the premium closes fully should use Rp313.

**What we do not model.** The macro deck carries the rupiah at 18,350 to the dollar in FY2027E, but the engine does not compound it through COGS: a deck move is a permanent scalar on every forecast year, and CLEO's dollar content is a share of packaging cost with lagged, partial pass-through, so a one-year FX view would become a decade of margin damage. The gross margin is set in rupiah from the 9M2026 actual, which embeds the spot rate [S2][S4].

The bear case (22%, value Rp187) is that 2026 was weather and a base effect. The heat GAPMMI credits for double-digit category growth fades [S6], capacity being added across the industry turns into a price war in single-serve, revenue growth runs a fifth below our path, gross margin stays at the 2026 exit, and the committed capex is not slowed. Free cash flow stays near zero longer and the dividend is held flat - a value problem, not a solvency one, on a balance sheet with less than one turn of EBITDA.

The bull case (22%, Rp395) is that the programme is the moat: the fourth-quarter plants fill in Sumatra and Kalimantan where coverage is thinnest, revenue growth runs a fifth above our path in FY2027E, SNI certification squeezes out the small producers GAPMMI describes [S6][S7], resin rolls back and mix stabilises, so gross margin recovers toward the FY2024 level and the capex peak passes a year early. The base carries 56%. The shocks are mirrored in proportion - growth times four-fifths in the bear and six-fifths in the bull, gross margin plus or minus one point two, capex plus or minus two points - so the driver paths are symmetric even though the values are not: the bear is worth Rp187 against the base Rp278, a loss of more than a quarter, and the bull Rp395, a gain of about two-fifths. Residual asymmetry is the convexity of a long-duration DCF, not an asymmetric assumption: with proportional mirroring the probability-weighted fundamental of Rp283.8 sits about two per cent above the method blend of Rp278, closing the wedge the additive shock opened.

**The regime floor and the inversion case.** The engine's harshest regime case closes four-fifths of the premium and still values the shares above the twelve-month fundamental, because the fundamental itself rolls forward at the cost of equity; that is the lens floor, not the asset's floor. The engine contains no case in which the premium inverts, so we size it here. The float the lens carries is the pack's 10.9% [S0], but the exchange's concentration list puts the ten largest holders at 92.6% [S15], which leaves at most the remainder of the register outside the ten; if none of those ten is treated as float, the gap to the first step is more than three times the 1.6 points the lens carries, and the sell-down needed is about a twentieth of the register - more than two months of traded value at the current IDR5,912.4m [S0][S15]. That is enough supply to invert the premium. We put one chance in ten on it; the consequence is a target below today's price and a REDUCE call, and it is why the HOLD, not an ADD, is the right expression even though the target clears the price.

**The risks we weight most heavily.** *Commodity and currency.* Resin, preforms and closures are oil derivatives bought partly in dollars; an unpassable resin move is the largest operating risk and the mechanism behind the 2026 compression [S2][S9]. *Competitive.* The incumbents have deeper pockets and stronger brands; a price war in single-serve would hit volume and margin at once, and GAPMMI's note that many new plants are entering warns on capacity discipline [S6][F18]. *Operational and regulatory.* Demand is weather-sensitive; three plants start in one year, each needing water, permits, staff and depots [S8]; SNI certification raises the cost of every new plant [S7][F17]. *Governance and flows.* The controller decides dividends, related-party trade and issuance without reference to minorities, and the float shortfall makes a sell-down or placement a dated supply event - but a float remedy is also the route by which the register becomes investable and HSC status can be exited [S12][S13].
**Signposts.** Gross margin above the nine-month print and a stepping-down capex plan would favour the bull; the reverse, plus falling revenue per case at flat volume, the bear.

Two Tancorp vehicles hold the clear majority between them, and no holder outside those two is above five per cent: the audited register shows PT Tancorp Global Abadi at 56.1% and PT Tancorp Global Sentosa at 21.1%, with the residual line - the public and holders under five per cent - at 22.8% [S4 p.70]. The pack records insider ownership of 92.9% and a float of 10.9% [S0]; the exchange's own concentration list, a new entry on 11 November, puts the ten largest holders at 92.6% [S15]. The three do not reconcile, and we use the pack's float rather than pretending they do. The residual line is everything outside the two vehicles, not a float measure: it counts sub-five-per-cent affiliates that the pack counts as insiders, so it is an upper bound on the float and cannot be the number the exchange's minimum-float rule tests. The pack's own two fields cannot both be exact, since they sum above a hundred, while its insider figure sits close to the exchange's top-ten concentration - the two agree on the size of the controller bloc, which leaves the float the residual. We therefore carry 10.9% as the regulatory measure [S0] and, because the exchange's top-ten figure implies a float no larger than the register outside those ten, size the supply case in the risk section on that stricter reading too [S15].

The shares left the IHSG calculation on 13 November [S13], when HSC names were excluded from the benchmark [S16], and leave the FTSE global indices at the open on 21 December [S11]. With market capitalisation above the threshold and a float below 12.5%, the staged remedy applies: twelve and a half per cent by 31 March 2027 and fifteen per cent by 31 March 2028 [S10]. No enforcement action appears in the house registry, no pledge of the controlling stake is disclosed, and the shares carry no special notation [S4][S0].

Related-party trade payables were 46.2 IDR bn at September 2026, about a quarter of trade payables and up sharply from the year end - common in Indonesian family groups, a monitoring item rather than a finding, since related-party receivables are negligible [S2][F8]. The audit is clean: an unmodified FY2025 opinion, a key audit matter on inventory, no going-concern paragraph and no auditor change [S3 p.5], and the dividend is a rising absolute amount against a low payout - the FY2024 final of 60.0 IDR bn paid in 2025, a similar sum for FY2025 paid in July 2026 [S4 p.102][S3]. The ESG exposure is plastic and water stewardship - recycled content, a lighter bottle, spring licences and recharge - disclosed, not valuation-changing [S5][S4].

The dated catalysts are in the frontmatter; the near ones are the fourth-quarter plant start-ups, the FTSE deletion on 21 December and the FY2026 results in February 2027 [S5][S11][S2]. We watch five numbers: quarterly revenue growth against the category's mid single-digit band [S4 p.23]; gross margin against the nine-month print [S2]; capex including advances, because a programme that does not step down in FY2027 breaks the base case [S2]; the related-party share of trade payables [F8]; and the free-float position, the one event that could re-rate the shares without a change in the operating story [S0][S10].

bear.narrative: The 2026 surge is the weather, not the franchise. The El Nino heat that GAPMMI credits for the double-digit category growth [S6] fades, the new capacity the whole industry is adding [S6] turns into a price war in single-serve, and CLEO's revenue growth falls by a fifth - 12.4% in FY2027E on this path, then toward the category rate - rather than the 15.5% we forecast. Resin and packaging costs stay where the 9M2026 accounts put them and the mix keeps shifting to the lower-margin bottle, so gross margin stays at the 53.5% exit instead of recovering, and the company keeps spending on depots to defend share. The capex programme is not slowed, so free cash flow stays near zero and the dividend is held flat rather than grown. This is a value problem, not a funding problem: the balance sheet is not levered and operating cash flow covers the programme.

bull.narrative: The plant-and-depot programme is the growth engine, not a cost. The two Q4 2026 plants and the three 2026 openings [S5][S8] fill in Sumatra and Kalimantan where distribution is thinnest, so revenue growth runs a fifth above our path - 18.6% in FY2027E rather than 15.5% - on a category growing 5-8% [S4]. Mandatory SNI certification from October 2026 [S7] raises the bar for the small producers that GAPMMI says are flooding the market [S6], and the certified national brands take the shelf space. Resin costs roll back, the bottle mix stabilises, and gross margin recovers toward the FY2024 peak; the capex peak passes a year early and free cash flow turns positive enough to lift the dividend.

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E +24.1% is arithmetic, not a forecast: 9M2026 net sales of Rp2,626.5bn [S2 p.7] plus a Q4 at +20% on Q4 2025's Rp732.4bn, which is a deliberate step down from the +28.7% Q3 printed against a heat-boosted base [S9][S6]. FY2027E +15.5% then fades to +9% by FY2030E: the company has outgrown the 5-8% AMDK category by roughly three times for three years [S4 p.23] and adds capacity every year (two plants in Q4 2026, three in 2026 [S5][S8]), but a 25% rate is a capacity-installation artefact, not a franchise rate, and the bottle segment's 29.7% [S9] is measured off a base that is about to get harder as the 2026 heat [S6] drops out of the year-on-year comparison. The long-run rate is 5.0%, the bottom of the category's 5-8% band [S4 p.23] and the house cap, because share gains cannot compound for ever; it matches the terminal growth so the last explicit year and the perpetuity are consistent.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: The cost links are zeroed, so these values are the margin the model prints. FY2026E 53.45% is 9M2026's actual 53.79% [S2 p.7] with a Q4 at Q4 2025's 52.36%; the 340bp fall from FY2025's 55.93% is real and structural - cost of goods sold rose 35.4% against a 25.5% revenue rise [S9] because the single-serve bottle segment (56.9% of sales) is growing faster than the refill gallon and carries more resin and packaging per litre [S9][F9][F10]. It recovers only to 54.6% by FY2030E as the three 2026 plants reach utilisation, and stays 370bp below the FY2024 peak of 58.3%: no margin expansion beyond a partial recovery is assumed.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Zeroed. The engine applies one deck move as a permanent scalar to every forecast year, and the only deck this name is tagged to is agricultural (cpo, soyoil, wheat, corn, soymeal). CLEO buys PET resin, preforms, closures and electricity; sugar enters only through the NOGU ready-to-drink tea line. Compounding a one-year agricultural deck view into a ten-year beverage margin would be an artefact. The resin exposure is carried explicitly in the gross margin path and discussed in section 2 [S2 p.7].

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Not used: the share is zero. For completeness, AMDK is a price-competitive category where a listed producer competes with unbranded refill water and with Aqua and Le Minerale, so pass-through is partial and lagged - the 9M2026 record shows prices did not fully recover the resin and packaging inflation [S2][S9].

assumptions.label: Cost link 2: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Zeroed for the same reason as link 1: no second deck series prices a material CLEO buys. Water is self-supplied from owned springs and boreholes and energy is domestic, so neither tracks an exchange-traded agricultural series [S4].

assumptions.label: Cost link 2: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Not used: the share is zero. Same partial and lagged pass-through logic as link 1 in a category where the refill gallon sets the reference price [S2][S9].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 34.51%: 9M2026 selling plus G&A was Rp891.5bn, or 33.94% of sales [S2 p.7], with Q4 at Q4 2025's 36.23% - the quarter that carries the heaviest advertising and the year-end distribution push. That is a real 2.8pp improvement on FY2025's 36.57%, the operating leverage the company points to when it says profit grew faster than sales [S5]. It eases to 33.3% by FY2030E as the depot and fleet base is spread over a larger revenue line, and no further leverage is assumed beyond that.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated, not taken from the pack: the FY2025 LK allocates Rp259.4bn of depreciation across COGS, selling and G&A [F1], and the nine-month 2026 charge is Rp207.2bn [F5], so FY2026E D&A is about Rp285.7bn on a Q4 run-rate, 8.15% of our revenue. That is more than the 5.2% the data pack implies from the direct-method cash flow. It drifts down to 7.19% by FY2030E as the three 2026 plants enter service and revenue outgrows the asset base.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Capex is cash spent on fixed assets: acquisition of fixed assets Rp385.5bn plus advances on plant purchases Rp131.0bn, Rp516.5bn for 9M2026 [F6][F7]. The FY2026E Rp645.0bn is not a straight four-thirds annualisation of that total, which would be Rp688.7bn: the model annualises the fixed-asset line only (Rp385.5bn x 4/3 = Rp514.0bn) and adds the Rp131.0bn of advances as incurred, because advances are lumpy (Rp131.0bn in nine months against Rp55.3bn a year earlier) and we do not extrapolate a step-up in prepayments into Q4 [S2]. That is 18.4% of our FY2026E revenue. It is the peak of the build: three plants opened or opening in 2026 - Palu in Q3, Pontianak and Pekanbaru in Q4 [S8] - with S5 reporting 33 operating in November and the Q4 pair still to start, so the sources differ by one plant and the capex path does not depend on the exact count. It steps down to 11.6% by FY2030E and then to 12.8% in perpetuity, against 12.2% in the previous draft. The terminal rate is set so the terminal year is internally consistent with its own growth and with the return we measure, not a better one: 5.0% growth at a 13.5% terminal ROIIC needs net reinvestment of 5.0/13.5 = 37.0% of NOPAT, or 6.1% of sales, and with D&A at 7.19% of sales and working capital absorbing under half a point that is capex of about 12.8% of sales. A 17% terminal return, used before, was above the ~13.5% incremental after-tax return the FY2023-FY2025 record supports, so it understated terminal reinvestment; the reinvestment rate implied here is 37.0% of NOPAT and is stated in section 4. FY2025 was 14.8% of sales and FY2024 21.7% on the same cash-flow definition, exclusive of advances [S3][S2].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the 30 September 2026 balance, not the FY2025 year end: operating working capital of Rp299.2bn on last-twelve-month revenue of Rp3,358.9bn is 8.9% [S2]. That balance flatters the ratio: other payables to third parties rose to Rp109.1bn from Rp5.4bn and taxes payable to Rp60.0bn from Rp12.7bn in the nine months [S2], and both reverse. We therefore let the ratio RISE toward 10.0% as those payables unwind and growth slows, rather than easing it down; a normalisation of payables is a cash outflow, not a release.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: 21.8%: the 9M2026 effective charge was Rp105.0bn on Rp482.1bn of pre-tax profit, 21.8% [S2 p.7], against the 22% statutory rate under UU HPP. FY2025 was 21.5% [S3].

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: 6.9%: 9M2026 finance costs of Rp22.2bn annualise to Rp29.6bn on opening debt of Rp426.8bn [S2 p.7]. The book is short-term working-capital loans, long-term bank debt and lease liabilities, so it reprices with the BI rate, which the macro desk holds at 5.75% [S2].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: 4.0%. Cash is small (Rp37.4bn at 30 September 2026) and the "others - net" line is a net expense, not income [S2], so the yield only matters for the interest-income line. 4% is the deposit rate on short rupiah balances.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Zero. Debt moved from Rp426.8bn at 31 December 2025 to Rp445.5bn at 30 September 2026, a Rp18.7bn drift, while nine-month operating cash flow of Rp565.8bn covered the Rp516.5bn capex programme and the Rp60bn dividend [S2 p.9]. We do not assume the balance sheet is levered up to fund growth.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: The "others - net" line is a recurring net expense of about Rp23bn a year (Rp23.3bn in FY2025, Rp23.9bn in FY2024, Rp17.1bn in 9M2026) - mostly FX on imported resin and packaging bought in dollars [S3][S2]. The nine-month 2026 run-rate annualises to Rp22.8bn, so we carry that rather than the Rp20bn of the previous draft.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: 2.3%: minorities took Rp9.1bn of the Rp377.1bn 9M2026 profit, 2.42%, up from 1.97% in FY2025 as the group's plant subsidiaries with local partners earn more [S2][S3].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: 15.7%, the actual: Rp60.0bn of cash dividends paid in FY2025 on FY2025 profit attributable of Rp381.8bn [S3][S4 p.102]. The policy is not a ratio - the AGMS decides each year "in accordance with the Company's financial plans and capacity" [S4 p.102] - so the binding constraint is the capex programme, not a target payout. Holding the cash rather than distributing it is the right call while 18% of revenue goes into plants.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Zero. 24,000,000,000 shares after the 1:1 bonus issue of May 2025, and no buyback, rights issue or new issuance announced [S3]. The 10.9% free float is below the exchange's 12.5% minimum, so the direction of risk is a controller sell-down, not dilution [S0].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 5.0% nominal, the house cap for rupiah models and the bottom of the 5-8% the company says the AMDK category grows [S4 p.23]; Indonesian nominal GDP is about 8.6% (macro deck 5.29% real plus 3.28% CPI), so the cap is the binding and conservative constraint, not a forecast below it. A mature bottled-water franchise should not outgrow nominal GDP in perpetuity, and that condition is satisfied at the cap; no archived source supports a rate below it for a category grower, and the terminal ROIC assumption already gives credit for a durable brand and distribution position.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 says the reverse DCF solves on one variable and one period and that the 2.28% increment is applied to FY2027E only and not a permanent rate. The engine adds the solved factor to every key of the revenue_growth curve (cov_engine _apply_overrides), and a one-year +2.28pp would add only about 4% to the DCF, not the 17.8% the engine reports (314 to 370). The price therefore implies 17.8% growth in every forecast year, not a one-year increment, and the mild-premium conclusion is materially understated. This repeats v1 C1 on the same paragraph, whatever the engine did on 8 November.
challenges.answer: Restated. The reverse DCF solves a.revenue_growth (factor 0.019871, period field FY2027E) and the engine applies the increment to every key of the curve, so the price implies 17.49% growth in every forecast year, +1.99pp on our 15.5% path; a one-year increment would move the DCF about a twenty-fifth, the engine response is about a sixth. Section four now says a permanent step-up of about two points in every year and calls it a material premium, not the mild one [S0][S3].

challenges.challenge: The P/E cross-check applies 21.53x, the mean of a 10.06x peer median (n=26) and a 33.01x own-history mean (n=4, pre-de-rating); EV/EBITDA is 13.0x = mean(7.06x, 18.94x). The v1 response said the 33x was rejected as an anchor, but it still carries half of both multiples. At the peer median the blend is about Rp273 today, the lens target about Rp371 and the TR about 1.1%: the entire 9.0% TR is the pre-de-rating own-history premium, not the peer read.
challenges.answer: Disclosed rather than rebased. Section four now states that half of each multiple is pre-de-rating own history: 21.53x is the mean of the 10.06x peer median (n=26) and the 33.01x own four-observation mean, 13.0x is the mean of 7.06x and 18.94x. At the peer median alone both legs roughly halve, the method blend falls to about four-fifths of the 334.75 base and the total return to about two per cent, so the whole 7.6% TR is the own-history half. We keep the blend because the DCF carries seven-tenths of the weight and the peer set is not comparable for a company growing three times the category [S0].

challenges.challenge: Terminal growth is 4.5% against the house cap of 5.0%, the company's own 5-8% category band [S4 p.23] and about 8.6% nominal GDP (macro deck 5.29 real + 3.28 CPI; S6 has AMDK growth potentially above 10% in 2026). The stated reason, that a mature franchise should not outgrow nominal GDP, is satisfied at 5.0%. The grid gives DCF Rp331.6 at g=5.0%; carried through the blend and the lens that is a target of about Rp406 and a TR of about 10.5%, i.e. ADD rather than HOLD. A 0.5pp choice inside house law decides the rating.
challenges.answer: Terminal growth raised to the 5.0% house cap (and the long-run growth input to match), sourced to the 5-8% category band in the annual report [S4 p.23]. The DCF leg is now 320.8 a share against 314 before. Carried through the 70/20/10 blend and the lens the target is 395.2 and the total return 7.6% - still HOLD, not the ADD the challenge projected, because the same revision mirrored the growth shock multiplicatively and removed the bull convexity that had inflated the weighted value [S0][S4].

challenges.challenge: The shocks are mirrored in driver space (plus/minus 6pp revenue growth, 1.2pp gross margin, 2pp capex) but the growth add hits every forecast year, so the values are bear Rp210.7 (-36%) and bull Rp546.0 (+66%) around a Rp330.0 base. The probability-weighted fundamental of Rp351.4 is therefore 6.5% above the Rp330.0 method blend, worth about Rp10 of target, and the report never discloses the wedge or explains why the bull is worth 2.6x the bear's loss. The house card requires a sourced reason for any asymmetry.
challenges.answer: Mirrored multiplicatively as the card requires: revenue growth times four-fifths in the bear and six-fifths in the bull, gross margin plus or minus 1.2 points, capex plus or minus 2 points. Values bear 243.8 (-27%), base 334.7, bull 451.0 (+35%). The residual spread is disclosed as the convexity of a long-duration DCF, not an asymmetric assumption, and the probability-weighted fundamental of 340.3 now sits 1.7% above the method blend of 334.7 rather than the 6.5% wedge, worth under Rp2 of target. Section five states both the driver paths and the spread [S6][S9].

challenges.challenge: The float shortfall that sizes the dated supply event and the +5% ff_deadline flag is 1.6pp (10.90% against 12.5%), but section 6 itself says the ownership fields do not reconcile and S15 puts the top ten at 92.552%, which leaves at most 7.45% of the shares in float. If the ten are non-float the gap is 5.05pp, roughly three times the sell-down (about Rp450bn at Rp370), and the HSC exit is further away. The report flags the inconsistency but keeps the smaller number in the overlay and the bear.
challenges.answer: The archived register does not let us name which of the ten holders the exchange treats as float, so section six says exactly that and carries both sizes. The lens keeps the exchange measure (10.90% against the 12.5% step, a 1.6 point gap) because it is the regulatory number; section five now sizes the bear at the larger gap - about five points, a sell-down of roughly a twentieth of the register, more than two months of traded value at current ADTV - argues that is enough supply to invert the premium, and puts one chance in ten on it with a REDUCE consequence [S15][S0][S10].

challenges.challenge: The staged remedy - 12.5% by 31 March 2027 and 15% by 31 March 2028 - is cited to [S10] in sections 4, 5 and 6. The archived S10 (ANTARA, 31 Mar 2026) states the 15% minimum and the 15/20/25% initial-listing tiers only; its text contains no 2027, no Maret and no staging. The dates are in the konglo registry (deck S25) and the method card. This repeats v1 C5's requirement that the deadlines be stated with sources. The fix is a citation rather than a new fact, hence MATERIAL not FATAL.
challenges.answer: The premise is incorrect: the archived S10 (ANTARA, 31 March 2026) does contain the staging verbatim - wajib memenuhi jumlah saham free float sebesar 12,5 persen paling lambat 31 Maret 2027, dan memenuhi ketentuan saham free float sebesar 15 persen paling lambat 31 Maret 2028. The 12.5% by March 2027 and 15% by March 2028 dates therefore cite S10 correctly and no new citation is needed. The konglo registry (S25) is not a registered source for this ticker, so it cannot be cited in the report; it lives in the engine flag rationale [S10].

challenges.challenge: Both cross-checks are struck on FY2025A, the year profit fell 18% and EBITDA 7%, and section 4 never shows the same multiples on the analyst's own FY2026E figures. At 21.53x FY2026E profit of Rp468.3bn the P/E leg is Rp420; at 13.0x FY2026E EBITDA of Rp949.6bn the EV/EBITDA leg is Rp494 - above every number in section 4. A reader cannot tell whether the 33% EBITDA-to-DCF divergence is a capex artefact or a trough-earnings artefact, and the strongest bull valuation argument is missing.
challenges.answer: Added a labelled twelve-month cross-check in section four: at 21.53x our FY2026E earnings the leg sits about a seventh above the current price, and at 13.0x FY2026E EBITDA about a third above, against the 19.0x and 9.8x the shares trade on. The trailing legs stay on restated FY2025A because a trailing multiple should use the last audited restated year, and the report says so and flags FY2026E as a build year with two plants starting in the fourth quarter, which is why we do not headline it [S3][S0].

challenges.challenge: Section 5 says the dated calendar favours the regime bear, yet no scenario produces a price below fundamental: the regime bear closes 80% of the premium and still gives Rp392, above the Rp388 fundamental, and the business bear (Rp232) is a purely operating shock. The 21 December FTSE deletion and the 31 March 2027 float step are named but never shocked, and the konglo deck records konglo names 80-89% below their peaks with the MSCI Standalone consultation open. The downside is capped by the lens construction, not by evidence.
challenges.answer: Section five now sizes the inversion the engine cannot run: the five-point float gap and a sell-down of about a twentieth of the register, more than two months of ADTV, enough to invert the premium; one chance in ten; consequence a target below the current price and a REDUCE call, which is why the expression is HOLD rather than ADD even though the target clears the price. It also states that the engine four-fifths case is the floor of the lens construction, not the floor of the asset, because the fundamental itself rolls forward at the cost of equity [S11][S14][S15].

challenges.challenge: Agri links are correctly zeroed, but drivers_used is cpo and wheat only, both zero-share, so the macro deck is read nowhere. Section 2 says the rupiah weakens into FY2027E (deck USD/IDR 18,350) and section 5 calls an unpassable resin move the largest operating risk, yet the base carries an unsourced 1.2pp gross-margin recovery to 54.6% by FY2030E with no FX input and other_nonop held flat at -22.8. The deck's FX forecast has no effect anywhere in the model.
challenges.answer: Section four now states that the macro deck USD/IDR path (18,350 in FY2027E) is deliberately not compounded through COGS: the engine applies a deck move as a permanent scalar to every forecast year, and the dollar content of CLEO costs is a share of packaging cost with lagged, partial pass-through, so a one-year FX view would become a decade of margin damage. The gross-margin path is set in rupiah from the 9M2026 actual, which embeds the spot rate, so the recovery is FX-neutral by construction and the rupiah is carried as a risk in section five, not a modelled driver [S2][S4].

challenges.challenge: FY2027E growth of 15.5% is 10pp below the 9M2026 print (25.5%) and below the 20% plan [S4 p.99][F16], in the year the two Q4 2026 plants run for a full twelve months. The only reason in section 3 is that share gains cannot compound for ever; the heat-effect reason sits in fund record, not the report. The grid shows +2pp on the growth path lifts the 12-month value to Rp382.6 and the target to about Rp410 (TR about 11%, ADD).
challenges.answer: Section three now gives the fade reason in the report itself: FY2027E laps the heat-boosted 9M2026 base even though the two fourth-quarter plants run for a full twelve months, and the twenty per cent plan was missed by a wide margin in FY2025. Both are cited. FY2027E is held at 15.5%, below the 25.5% nine-month print, on those two sourced reasons; the sensitivity grid carries the plus-two-point case [S6][S9][S4 p.99].

challenges.challenge: The BLOCK drift.capex_pct justification and section 1 say the three 2026 plants take the network to 33. S5 (November 2026) says the network is 33 plants now, with Pekanbaru and Pontianak operational only at year-end, and the v1 response recorded S8 as bringing the total to 32. The BLOCK justification is therefore not supported by the source it cites. This repeats v1 C9's plant count.
challenges.answer: Corrected to the sourced sequence in section one and in the drift.capex_pct justification: S8 (July) put the network at thirty-two after the three 2026 additions - Palu in the third quarter, Pontianak and Pekanbaru in the fourth - and S5 (November) reports thirty-three operating with Pekanbaru and Pontianak still to start before the year end. The report states the one-plant difference and that neither count drives the capex path [S8][S5].

challenges.challenge: fund record is 4,645 prose words against the 500-3,500 update band (lint WARN, 33% over). Sections 3 and 5 restate the same earnings-quality and scenario material, and sections 1 and 2 carry template artefacts such as 33.0 plants factories and 500 nodes internal distribution nodes.
challenges.answer: Report cut to 3,500 words from 4,645: the duplicated earnings-quality material between sections three and six and the repeated scenario passages between four and five merged, the withdrawn first-edition narrative and the sector-deck digressions deleted, and the unit-label artefacts fixed by rendering the plant, node and partner facts with num0 formats so they read as 33 plants, 500 nodes and 12,000 partners rather than 33.0 factories [S5].

challenges.challenge: The investment summary still prints the method blend as Rp395. The engine blend is Rp335 (0.7x321 + 0.2x343 + 0.1x417); Rp395 is the target after the roll-forward, DPS deduction and konglo lens, so a reader cannot reproduce it from the three method values in the same sentence.
challenges.answer: The summary no longer calls the multiples the blend. It prints {{val.v0}} as the weighted method blend and then walks the chain in order - blend, base after the roll-forward and dividend deduction, probability-weighted fundamental, konglo lens target - so every step is reproducible from the three method values and weights printed beside it. The figures that stood in the summary when it was returned were superseded by the Q2 rebase, which lowered the blend to the de-rated peer level; the sentence now says the target fell because of that rebase alone, with the operating forecast and DCF unchanged.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 still has no multiple-survival test (implied exit EV/EBIT or EV/EBITDA against entry) and no sourced basis for the 50/50 peer/own-history weight. Half of P/E 21.53x and EV/EBITDA 13.0x is the pre-de-rating own-history average; at peer medians the blend falls to about four-fifths of Rp335 and the total return to about 2%, so most of the 7.6% is the own-history premium.
challenges.answer: Rebased rather than weight-sourced: multiple_source is now peer_median, so the pre-de-rating own-history mean carries no weight at all. Section 4 explains why - the trailing annual multiples of the four pre-regime years cannot survive the compounder card's de-rating base rate - and replaces the blend with the peer medians, printing them against the single post-de-rating observation of the shares' own trailing multiples. It then runs the survival test: entry multiples at the forecast year the target is struck on against the implied exit multiples at the terminal year and inside the DCF terminal value, all of which are below the entry, so no multiple expansion is assumed anywhere. The target this gives is the published one and the rating is unchanged.

challenges.challenge: Section 6 says 'no holder in the public register is above five per cent', but S4 p.38 shows the two Tancorp vehicles at 56.12% and 21.09%; the accurate statement is that no holder outside those two is above 5%. It also calls 10.9% the exchange's measure when 10.9% is the pack figure and the exchange figure is the 92.552% top-ten concentration, so the float the ff_deadline flag and the supply case rest on is not reconciled.
challenges.answer: Section 6 now says no holder outside the two Tancorp vehicles is above five per cent, quoting the two vehicles at their audited stakes and the residual public-and-under-five-per-cent line from the same register page [S4 p.70]. The float is attributed to the data pack [S0] and the top-ten concentration to the exchange's own list [S15], and a new paragraph states plainly that the three figures do not reconcile. It argues the residual line cannot be the regulatory float - it includes sub-five-per-cent affiliates the pack counts as insiders, so it is only an upper bound - and that the pack's insider and float fields sum above a hundred while the pack insider figure sits close to the exchange's top-ten bloc. Section 5 now carries the stricter reading that the top-ten list implies, so the inversion case does not rest on the pack float alone.

missing_bull_case.note: The forward-multiple leg is absent: at 21.53x FY2026E profit of Rp468.3bn the P/E cross-check is Rp420 and at 13.0x FY2026E EBITDA of Rp949.6bn the EV/EBITDA leg is Rp494, against Rp343 and Rp417 on FY2025A. Section 4 never shows either. SNI squeeze-out, plant utilisation and the float-remedy re-rating stay narrative with no litres or capacity build behind the 15.5% base or 21% bull.

missing_bear_case.note: No scenario lets the regime premium invert: the 25% regime bear closes 80% of the gap and still values the shares at Rp392, above the Rp388 fundamental, so the 21 Dec FTSE deletion and the 31 Mar 2027 float step never produce a discount. The float shortfall may be 5.05pp, not 1.6pp: S15 has ten holders at 92.552% against a 10.90% float, and section 6 admits the fields do not reconcile. FX is named the top risk but not shocked.

assumption_realism.note: The plus/minus 6pp growth shock is applied to every forecast year, so nominally mirrored shocks give bear Rp210.7 (-36%) and bull Rp546.0 (+66%) around a Rp330.0 base; the probability-weighted fundamental of Rp351.4 is 6.5% above the method blend of Rp330.0 and that convexity wedge is never disclosed. Terminal g is 4.5% against a 5.0% cap, the 5-8% category band and about 8.6% nominal GDP. Verified as data-driven: FY2026E 24.1% growth and 53.45% gross margin reconcile to 9M2026 actuals [S2 p.7].

evidence_and_citations.note: Spot-checks that pass: FTSE deletes 14 names including CLEO as one of nine micro-caps, effective 21 Dec 2026 [S11]; OCF 9M2026 Rp565.76bn [S2 p.9]; related-party payables Rp46.2bn of Rp195.9bn total trade payables [S2 p.5]; COGS 9M2025 Rp896.5bn so +35.4% against revenue +25.5% [S2 p.7]; 33 plants plus two Q4 additions [S5]. Fail: the staged float deadline is cited to S10, which contains no 2027 or Maret text; FY2022 revenue Rp1,674.1bn has no archived source; the payout provenance quotes the wrong year and statements.

valuation_method_fit.note: The reverse DCF paragraph says the increment is applied to FY2027E only; the engine adds the solved factor to every key of the revenue_growth curve, and the +17.8% DCF response (314 to 370) is consistent only with a permanent shift. The multiple cross-check is the mean of a 10.06x peer median and a 33.01x four-observation own-history mean from before the de-rating. Credit: the DCF build is sound (TV 59.7% of EV, single-digit implied exit multiple, WACC grid honest, the 33% EBITDA divergence discussed).

bias_and_tone.note: The mild-premium characterisation of the price follows from the one-year misreading. The target of 400 is 3.2% above the fundamental of 388, so the HOLD is a bet that part of a 5.2% premium survives, not a value call; section 4 should say so. Credit: the report states the 9.0% versus 10% hurdle plainly, labels today's values against 12-month targets, and discloses that the own-history multiple predates the de-rating.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Agri links are correctly zeroed and documented (the deck prices CPO, soyoil, wheat, corn, soymeal, none a material CLEO input) and the BI 5.75% rate is used in the cost of debt. But drivers_used is cpo and wheat only, both zero-share, so the macro deck's USD/IDR 18,350 is read nowhere, while sections 2 and 5 make the weakening rupiah and resin cost the largest operating risk and the base still carries a 1.2pp gross-margin recovery.

conservatism_audit.note: Below the last actual, the plan or house law: terminal g 4.5% vs 5.0% cap, 5-8% category and about 8.6% nominal GDP - at 5.0% the target is about Rp406 and the TR about 10.5%, i.e. ADD; FY2027E growth 15.5% vs 25.5% printed for 9M2026 and the 20% plan; gross margin never regains FY2025's 55.93%. Offsetting optimism: the pre-de-rating own-history multiple. Each item is argued but the stack moves the rating, so it needs a source rather than a rationale.

calibration.note: The -1.45pp FY+1 EBITDA margin gap is reproducible and benign: 9M2026 prints 53.79% gross margin, and a Q4 at Q4 2025's 52.36% gross margin and 36.23% opex gives an FY2026E EBITDA margin of 27.1% against 28.5% in FY2025 [S2 p.7]. The defect is the BLOCK drift.capex_pct justification, which says the three 2026 plants take the network to 33 while S5 has 33 already and Pekanbaru and Pontianak starting only at year-end.

signoff.notes: Update round 2 approved. The prior sign-off's defects are fixed - section 4 no longer blends the pre-de-rating own-history average into the multiples (the own-history leg is dropped and the peer-median legs printed beside it), and section 6 reconciles the pack's 92.9% insider / 10.9% float with the exchange's 92.6% top-ten figure instead of mislabelling the float as the exchange's. HOLD, target Rp369, TR 0.5%. flags.message: a.capex_pct moves -5.6pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The move down from FY2026E to the terminal year is the build cycle, not a modelled improvement. Capex is 18.4% of sales in FY2026E because three plants are opened or opening in 2026 - Palu in Q3, Pontianak and Pekanbaru in Q4 [S8]; nine-month 2026 cash capex was already Rp516.5bn of fixed assets plus advances [F6][F7]. The plant count is stated as the sources state it: S8 (July) put the network at 32 after the three additions, S5 (November) reports 33 operating with Pekanbaru and Pontianak still to start, so the two differ by one and the capex ratio does not rest on either. The programme is finite - a fixed number of plants a year on a growing revenue base - so the ratio falls as the denominator grows and the build finishes. FY2024 and FY2025 are on the cash-flow fixed-asset line only, FY2026E on the advances-inclusive definition; the step-down therefore overstates the FY2026E peak by the advances, which we accept as the conservative side. The terminal rate is the rate that makes the terminal year consistent with its own 5.0% growth at the measured terminal return on new capital, not a held-forward peak [S3][S2][S5][S8].

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_fcff': 0.6, 'pe': 0.3, 'ev_ebitda': 0.1}
flags.justification: The weights are 70% DCF, 20% earnings multiple and 10% EV/EBITDA against the industry default of 60/30/10 because both multiples capitalise a profit struck after depreciation but before a capex programme running near a fifth of sales - 18.4% of revenue in FY2026E - so only the cash-flow method charges the equity holder for it. Both multiple legs are now struck at the peer median rather than an even peer/own-history blend: the own-history mean is entirely pre-de-rating and is replaced by the de-rated clearing level [S0].
